before.quote:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let causal
curves be those of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]].

**(a) Convergent ends are extendible.** Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a future
causal curve and suppose $b:=\sup I<\infty$ and $\gamma(t)\to x\in M$ as
$t\to\sup I$. Then there is $\varepsilon>0$ and a future causal curve
$\tilde\gamma$ defined on $I\cup[b,b+\varepsilon)$ whose restriction to $I$
is $\gamma$. Consequently a future-inextendible causal curve whose domain is
bounded above does not converge at its upper end, and the dual statement
holds at the past end.

**(b) Maximal geodesics have no limit.** Let $(p,v)\in TM$ with $v\ne0$ and
let $\gamma_{p,v}:I_{p,v}\to M$ be the unique maximal geodesic with
$\gamma_{p,v}(0)=p$ and $\gamma_{p,v}'(0)=v$, as supplied by
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]] clause (a). Then
$\gamma_{p,v}(t)$ does not converge to any point of $M$ as $t\to\sup I_{p,v}$
or as $t\to\inf I_{p,v}$ (where convergence at an infinite end means
convergence as $t\to+\infty$ or $t\to-\infty$ respectively).

**(c) Segments lie on inextendible causal curves.** Let $\gamma:[t_0,t_1]\to M$
with $t_0<t_1$ be a future causal curve, or a past causal curve. Then there
is an inextendible causal curve $\hat\gamma:J\to M$ (same direction as
$\gamma$ in the case at hand) and a strictly increasing affine map
$\rho:[t_0,t_1]\to J$ with $\hat\gamma\circ\rho=\gamma$. In particular, any
two distinct points $p,q\in M$ with $p\le q$ and $p\ne q$ lie on a common
inextendible causal curve, and likewise for the past relation.

**(d) Cauchy sets are acausal.** Every Cauchy set of
[[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (c) is acausal in
the sense of clause (b) of that definition.

before.claim: 1.1 (The quotient model.) By [L1] and [L2] the hypotheses of the descent lemma are satisfied, so [L3] gives the time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$, the local isometry identity of (a) and the local charts with constant components. In each such chart, [L4] shows that the Christoffel symbols of the metric-selected connection vanish on the chart and hence that its curvature vanishes there; since the charts of the descent lemma cover $M$, the curvature vanishes on $M$ and the model is flat in the asserted sense. This proves (a).

2.1 (The closed timelike curve.) Define $\gamma(s):=q(o+se_0)$. Since $s\mapsto o+se_0$ is smooth and $q$ is smooth, $\gamma$ is smooth, and $\gamma(s+L)=q(o+(s+L)e_0)=q(o+se_0+Le_0)=q(o+se_0)=\gamma(s)$ because $Le_0\in\Lambda$. Its velocity is $\gamma'(s)=dq_{o+se_0}(\partial_0)$ by the chain rule, and by the local isometry identity $g(\gamma',\gamma')=\eta(\partial_0,\partial_0)=-1<0$ and $g(\gamma',N)=g(\gamma',dq(\partial_0))=\eta(\partial_0,\partial_0)=-1<0$; so every tangent is future timelike and the curve is a future timelike causal curve in the class of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. It is nonconstant: if $\gamma(s)=\gamma(0)=q(o)$ then $se_0\in\Lambda$, so $s=nL$ for some integer $n$, and for $0<s<L$ no such integer exists. Hence $\gamma|_{[0,L]}$ is a nonconstant closed future timelike curve, and by [[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (a) the model is neither chronological nor causal. This proves (b).

3.1 (Total viciousness.) Let $p,q\in M$ and choose lifts $\tilde p,\tilde q\in A$ of them, so that $q(\tilde p)=p$ and $q(\tilde q)=q$; such lifts exist because $q$ is surjective. Choose $n\in\mathbb Z$ with $nL>\bigl(x^0(\tilde q)-x^0(\tilde p)\bigr)+|z(\tilde q)-z(\tilde p)|_{\mathrm e}$ in the global inertial chart $x$; possible because the left side tends to $+\infty$. The displacement $(\tilde q+nLe_0)-\tilde p$ has time coordinate larger than the Euclidean norm of its spatial part, so it lies in the open future cone $C^+$; by [L5] the straight path $s\mapsto\tilde p+s\bigl((\tilde q+nLe_0)-\tilde p\bigr)$, $s\in[0,1]$, is a future timelike curve of the flat model, and composing with $q$ gives a smooth future timelike curve from $p$ to $q(\tilde q+nLe_0)=q(\tilde q)=q$, since $nLe_0\in\Lambda$. Hence $p\ll q$; taking $q=p$ exhibits the closed orbits, and taking $p\ne q$ shows that no two distinct points are achronal or acausal. This proves (c).

4.1 (No Cauchy set.) Let $S\subseteq M$ be a Cauchy set. By [L6] $S$ is acausal, so by step 3.1 it has at most one point. If $S=\{p\}$ for some $p$, let $\tilde p$ be a lift and consider the curve $\gamma_p(s):=q(\tilde p+se_0)$, which is a future timelike curve with $\gamma_p(s+L)=\gamma_p(s)$ and $\gamma_p(0)=p$, by the argument of step 2.1 applied at $\tilde p$. The parameter set $\{s\in\mathbb R:\gamma_p(s)\in S\}$ contains $0$ and $L$, two distinct parameters, so it is not a singleton and $\{p\}$ is not a Cauchy set. Since the empty set is not a Cauchy set either (it is met by no curve at all, while the definition requires exactly one meeting), no Cauchy set exists, and in particular no Cauchy hypersurface exists. This proves (d).
5.1 (Conclusion.) Part (a) is step 1.1, part (b) is step 2.1, part (c) is step 3.1, and part (d) is step 4.1; this completes the proof.
